evidence.statement: Citing Bloomberg, reports that Ras Laffan is loading LNG at roughly half its pre-war pace, with a 10-day average of 13-15 cargoes so far in November against about 11 in October, amid ongoing Hormuz disruption (Enterprise).
QatarEnergy restored LNG exports in September to about a third of pre-war levels, and at least 20 more cargoes have passed Hormuz since early September (Semafor, citing Bloomberg).

Much of Ras Laffan has been shut since the war began; Kpler put September LNG exports at 1.6 million tonnes, under a quarter of the pre-war average, with October on track for 0.6 million tonnes (Reuters, via Cyprus Mail).
Wood Mackenzie expected the North site back within a month of a restart; the strikes that damaged two trains hit the South site (The National).
QatarEnergy declared force majeure on its entire LNG output after missile and rocket attacks on Ras Laffan caused fires and extensive damage (Fox Business, citing Reuters).

Bloomberg reports that LNG loadings from Ras Laffan in early November were running at 13 to 15 shipments on a 10-day moving average, still roughly half the pre-war pace amid ongoing Strait of Hormuz disruptions (Bloomberg).
QatarEnergy restored LNG exports in September to about a third of pre-war levels, and at least 20 more cargoes have passed Hormuz since early September (Semafor, citing Bloomberg).

Much of Ras Laffan has been shut since the war began; Kpler put September LNG exports at 1.6 million tonnes, under a quarter of the pre-war average, with October on track for 0.6 million tonnes (Reuters, via Cyprus Mail).

Iranian strikes damaged Trains 4 and 6, removing 12.8 million tonnes a year and cutting the South site from 36 to 24 million tonnes a year; Wood Mackenzie expected it back by late summer at the earliest (The National).
QatarEnergy declared force majeure on its entire LNG output after missile and rocket attacks on Ras Laffan caused fires and extensive damage (Fox Business, citing Reuters).
Reuters reported that S&P Global Energy vessel tracking data showed eight laden LNG tankers left the Strait of Hormuz after loading at Das Island in October 2026 (Reuters).

Satellite images showed a tanker docked at Das Island on 2 September and another nearby; ADNOC appears to keep loading LNG, with tankers crossing Hormuz with transponders off. Gulf LNG exports remain far below pre-war levels (Bloomberg, via Energy Connects).
ADNOC Gas made temporary adjustments to its LNG production in response to shipping disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, and is handling commitments deal by deal (Reuters, via Baird Maritime).
